dossier.purpose: TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) is a compact, indentation-based text encoding of the JSON data model meant to reduce LLM prompt tokens (README.md:11-15). This repo (toon-format/toon) is the TypeScript reference implementation: library @toon-format/toon (encode/decode, line and event streaming), CLI @toon-format/cli (`toon`: JSON<->TOON, `--stats` token estimates), a VitePress docs site with a client-side playground, and a private benchmark harness (token counts; LLM retrieval accuracy). The format spec lives in a separate repo (SPEC.md:3). For the stated need 'which single tool measures provider usage from the local logs Claude Code and Codex write (input, output, cache-creation, cache-read tokens)': none. This project contains no such tool; it only estimates or tokenizes text size (packages/cli/src/conversion.ts:47-59; benchmarks/src/utils.ts:29-31).

claims.claim: TOON is 'a compact, human-readable encoding of the JSON data model that minimizes tokens and makes structure easy for models to follow'.
Sweet spot is uniform objects (in arrays or keyed by ID) at 'CSV-like compactness'; 'For deeply nested or non-uniform data, JSON may be more efficient.'
Use JSON programmatically and encode as TOON for LLM input: 'a drop-in, lossless representation of the JSON you already have'; 'deterministic, lossless round-trips'.
'The TOON format is stable, but also an idea in progress. Nothing's set in stone.'
`cat data.json | npx @toon-format/cli --stats` prints the TOON plus what the conversion saved, e.g. 'Token estimates: ~117 (JSON) -> ~66 (TOON)' and 'Saved ~51 tokens (-43.6%)'.
'Matches JSON's retrieval accuracy while using 42.6% fewer tokens' (TOON 72.2% vs JSON 71.4% accuracy).
Explicit [N] lengths and {fields} lists give models 'a clear schema to follow, improving parsing reliability'; structural-validation accuracy TOON 100% vs JSON 50%.

'When Not to Use TOON': deeply nested or non-uniform data (compact JSON often wins), semi-uniform arrays (savings shrink), purely tabular data (CSV is smaller; TOON has ~5-10% overhead), latency-critical use (measure TTFT and total time yourself).

Token counts use gpt-tokenizer o200k_base (GPT-5 tokenizer); other providers tokenize differently but 'relative differences between formats hold directionally'; savings are computed against 2-space-indented JSON; 'Actual savings vary by model and tokenizer'.

Benchmark design: 244 questions x 6 formats x 4 models (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, gemini-3.6-flash, gpt-5.4-nano, grok-4.5) = 5,856 LLM calls; reasoning disabled; temperature unset; Wilson 95% intervals reported.
Streaming: `encodeLines` is 'memory-efficient streaming for large data'; `decodeFromLines()` and `decodeStream()` are the streaming decode APIs; an encode `replacer` can drop sensitive fields.
CLI auto-detects encode/decode from file extension, supports stdin/stdout, and offers comma/tab/pipe delimiters that 'trade readability for fewer tokens'.
'Full-line # comments are stripped on decode'; 'Tab delimiters buy further token savings'; wrap data in ```toon code blocks for prompts.

Ecosystem: Tooner is an MCP proxy that converts JSON tool responses to TOON (third-party); implementations in other languages exist (separate repos); media type text/toon (provisional), .toon extension, UTF-8; MIT license.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or phone-home code found. Library and CLI sources (packages/toon/src, packages/cli/src) contain no network calls (grep for fetch/http/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket in packages/ found only URLs in package metadata, a comment and test strings) and no env-var, home-directory or directory-scanning reads (grep for process.env/homedir/readdir/glob found none). The docs playground is client-side: state lives in the URL hash, the tokenizer is imported in the browser, and there are no fetch calls (docs/.vitepress/theme/components/PlaygroundLayout.vue:147-152,170-182,237-239,266-268); docs search is local (docs/.vitepress/config.ts:98-100).

code.architecture: pnpm monorepo (pnpm-workspace.yaml:9-12): packages/toon (library), packages/cli (CLI), benchmarks (private), docs (private VitePress). Library: packages/toon/src/index.ts is the public API. Encode path: encode/normalize.ts (unknown -> JSON value: toJSON, Date, BigInt, Set/Map, -0, non-finite -> null, lone-surrogate rejection) -> encode/replacer.ts -> encode/encoders.ts (generator emitting lines in inline, tabular `key[N]{fields}:`, keyed-tabular `key[N:]{fields}:` or list form) with encode/tabular.ts (uniformity detection incl. nested field groups), encode/primitives.ts (quoting, headers) and encode/raw-string.ts. Decode path: decode/scanner.ts (indentation, BOM/CRLF, full-line '#' comments, tab rules) -> decode/line-reader.ts (one rule tree driven by sync or async sources) -> decode/decoders.ts (emits JsonStreamEvent) using decode/parser.ts (header and token parsing), decode/validation.ts (strict-mode count and blank-line checks) and decode/errors.ts (ToonDecodeError with line/source) -> decode/event-builder.ts (events -> value). shared/* holds escaping, literal checks and own-property helpers that are __proto__-safe. CLI: packages/cli/src/{entry,index,conversion,utils,errors,format-error,json-from-events,log}.ts using citty (args), ansis (color), tokenx (estimates); it imports library code by relative path (../../toon/src/index.ts), not as a package dependency. Build: tsdown per package. Benchmarks (benchmarks/src, benchmarks/scripts): faker-seeded generated datasets plus a real top-100 GitHub-repos JSON (benchmarks/src/datasets.ts:3,5-6,311-315), six format encoders (JSON, JSON compact, YAML, XML, CSV, TOON: benchmarks/src/formats.ts:29-72), question generators, LLM evaluation via the Vercel AI SDK (src/evaluate.ts), report generation (src/report.ts); results are committed under benchmarks/results/ and embedded into README/docs through automd:file markers (README.md:173,458; docs/guide/benchmarks.md:19,304).
code.packaging_and_release: Published to npm as two ESM-only packages, @toon-format/toon (files: dist; exports -> dist/index.mjs + .d.mts) and @toon-format/cli (files: bin, dist; bin `toon` -> bin/toon.mjs), both at 4.1.1 (packages/toon/package.json:4,26-35; packages/cli/package.json:4,18-31). Version bump via `bumpp -r` (package.json:17). .github/workflows/release.yml fires on `v*` tags (lines 3-6) on `ubuntu-slim` with `id-token: write` and `contents: write` (17-19): `npx changelogithub` creates the GitHub release notes (38-41), then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (43-44), `pnpm run build` (46-47), and `npm install -g npm@latest && pnpm -r publish --access public --no-git-checks` (49-50). No release binaries, checksums, signatures, SBOM or explicit provenance/attestation step appear in the repo (grep of .github for provenance/attest/cosign/sigstore/checksum/sha256/gpg/slsa: no match), so whether npm provenance is attached cannot be determined from the repo. The v4.1.1 ref is an annotated tag object that peels to the release commit (.git/packed-refs:2-3); tag signature not inspected. Docs are deployed separately to Cloudflare by .github/workflows/deploy.yml (wrangler deploy on pushes to main touching docs/** etc.).
code.tests_and_ci: Vitest (^4.1.10: package.json:30; no vitest/vite config files, defaults used) driven per package via `test` scripts (packages/toon/package.json:38; packages/cli/package.json:35; benchmarks/package.json:6). 16 test files: packages/toon/test (10: decode, decode-errors, decode-security, decodeStream, encode, encode-security, encodeLines, normalization, raw-string, replacer), packages/cli/test (5: cli, cli-process, errors, format-error, json-from-events), benchmarks/test (1: utils). About 250 literal it()/describe() call sites, plus fixture-driven cases generated at run time from the @toon-format/spec conformance fixtures (packages/toon/test/utils.ts:15-19; packages/toon/test/decode.test.ts:9-24; packages/toon/test/encode.test.ts:9-19). CLI tests run in-process and as a child process (packages/cli/test/utils.ts:85-157). CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml on push/PR to main, one job on `ubuntu-slim`, Node 24, 10-minute timeout, running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm run lint` (ESLint, @antfu/eslint-config), `pnpm run test:types` (`tsc --noEmit`) and `pnpm run test` (`pnpm -r test`); no OS or Node matrix, no coverage step. .github/workflows/pr-title.yml lints PR titles with commitlint (conventional commits, lowercase subject); deploy.yml builds and deploys the docs; release.yml publishes on tags. The LLM accuracy benchmark (needs API keys) and the benchmarks `verify` scripts (benchmarks/package.json:9-11) are not run by CI.
code.dependencies: No runtime `dependencies` in any manifest. Direct devDependency counts: package.json (root, private): 11; packages/toon/package.json: 1 (@toon-format/spec, used for conformance fixtures); packages/cli/package.json: 3 (ansis, citty, tokenx); benchmarks/package.json (private): 16 (incl. @ai-sdk/anthropic, google, openai, xai, provider; ai; gpt-tokenizer; @faker-js/faker; yaml; fast-xml-parser; csv-stringify; unstorage; ofetch; p-map; p-queue; @clack/prompts); docs/package.json (private): 9 (incl. vitepress, vitepress-plugin-llms, unocss, gpt-tokenizer, yaml). Lockfile pnpm-lock.yaml (lockfileVersion 9.0); packageManager pnpm@11.17.0 (package.json:6). pnpm-workspace.yaml sets `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` and limits dependency build scripts to @parcel/watcher and esbuild (lines 4-16). The CLI imports the library by relative source path rather than declaring it as a dependency (packages/cli/src/index.ts:2,6).
code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md (glob for SECURITY*, CONTRIBUTING*, CODEOWNERS, CHANGELOG* matched nothing). Spec section 15 'Security Considerations' is in the separate spec repo (docs/reference/spec.md:79-80). Library hardening is tested instead: own-property handling that is __proto__-safe (packages/toon/src/shared/object-utils.ts:3-33; packages/toon/test/decode-security.test.ts; packages/toon/test/encode-security.test.ts) and strict-mode decoding by default (docs/reference/api.md:614-629).

claim_checks.claim: 'Matches JSON's retrieval accuracy while using 42.6% fewer tokens' (README.md:146,225)
claim_checks.evidence: Arithmetic reproduces: 1 - 2,474/4,308 = 42.6% (README.md:215,218), and the code computes it as 1 - toon/json-pretty over per-dataset mean token counts of primer + encoded data (benchmarks/src/report.ts:25-44,222,246). But (a) the baseline is pretty-printed JSON; against JSON compact the same table gives 2,474 vs 2,892 tokens (README.md:215-216; derived ~14.5% fewer, my arithmetic); (b) accuracy 72.2% vs 71.4% sits inside the +/-2.8 Wilson intervals, which the README says are not statistically meaningful when they overlap (README.md:282); (c) the token counts are gpt-tokenizer counts of the prompt text, not provider-billed usage.

claim_checks.claim: 'deterministic, lossless round-trips' / 'drop-in, lossless representation of the JSON you already have' (README.md:15,147)
claim_checks.evidence: The encoder is a deterministic line generator (packages/toon/src/encode/encoders.ts:10-33) and decode(encode(x)) is tested (packages/toon/test/decode.test.ts:52-89; packages/toon/test/encode-security.test.ts:8-61). The docs qualify it as lossless 'after normalization' (docs/guide/getting-started.md:219; docs/reference/api.md:53-68,693-710): -0 -> 0, NaN/Infinity/undefined/function/symbol -> null, Date -> ISO string, BigInt beyond 2^53 -> quoted string (packages/toon/src/encode/normalize.ts:43-91). Numbers follow IEEE-754 doubles with silent rounding of large integers (docs/reference/api.md:343); JS reorders integer-like keys (docs/reference/api.md:635); lone surrogates make encode throw (normalize.ts:94-117). The CLI encodes via JSON.parse (packages/cli/src/conversion.ts:25), so the original JSON text formatting and number lexemes are not preserved. The repo has no mechanism to store or restore originals.

claim_checks.claim: CLI `--stats` prints token estimates and savings, e.g. '~117 (JSON) -> ~66 (TOON)', '-43.6%' (README.md:131-142)
claim_checks.evidence: The mechanism is verified: packages/cli/src/conversion.ts:47-59 calls tokenx `estimateTokenCount` on the raw input text (`jsonContent`, so the baseline depends on the input file's formatting) and on the TOON output, then prints 'Token estimates: ~A (JSON) -> ~B (TOON)' and 'Saved ~N tokens (-P%)'. docs/cli/index.md:145 calls them 'accurate token counts' while the same page and the code call them estimates (docs/cli/index.md:157,176; conversion.ts:58); this differs from the o200k_base tokenizer used by the benchmarks (benchmarks/src/utils.ts:2,29-31). cli.test.ts:272-289 only asserts that the text appears on stderr and stdout stays clean. tokenx internals were not inspected (no node_modules) and the example numbers were not re-run. It is not a provider-usage measurement: nothing reads provider responses or Claude Code/Codex logs.

claim_checks.claim: Explicit [N] lengths and {fields} lists improve parsing reliability and let strict mode detect truncation (README.md:148,295)
claim_checks.evidence: Deterministic side verified: strict mode (default true, packages/toon/src/index.ts:215) throws on count mismatches via assertExpectedCount (packages/toon/src/decode/validation.ts:8-21), used for inline arrays, tabular rows, keyed entries and list items (packages/toon/src/decode/decoders.ts:328,397,405,447,459,515); fixtures 'validation-errors' run in decode.test.ts:20. The LLM-reliability evidence is a small vendor-run sample: 5 YES/NO questions x 4 models = 20 evaluations per format (benchmarks/src/questions/structural-validation.ts:23-42; README.md:295,362-415). XML and CSV score 0/4 on the valid control and 4/4 on every corrupted variant (README.md:370-371,377-379,388-390,399-402,410-412), a pattern consistent with a constant NO answer.

claim_checks.claim: 'When Not to Use TOON': CSV is smaller on purely tabular data (~5-10% overhead); compact JSON often wins on nested/semi-uniform data (README.md:153-162)
claim_checks.evidence: Published outputs agree: flat track TOON is +6.0%, +8.7%, +2.6% vs CSV, total +5.9% (README.md:521,530,539,547); mixed track TOON is larger than JSON compact by +5.6% (orders), +19.9% (event logs), +6.7% (nested config), total +1.6% (README.md:469,477,485,508). The sign convention follows packages/benchmarks code: savingsPercent < 0 prints '+' (benchmarks/scripts/token-efficiency-benchmark.ts:47-56).

claim_checks.claim: Token counts use gpt-tokenizer o200k_base; 'relative differences between formats hold directionally' across providers (README.md:443,454,554)
claim_checks.evidence: The code calls the package default `encode` from gpt-tokenizer and does not name an encoding (benchmarks/src/utils.ts:2,29-31); 'o200k_base' rests on the gpt-tokenizer ^3.4.0 default (benchmarks/package.json:25), whose source was not inspected. Report counts use primer + encoded data text (benchmarks/src/report.ts:25-44). Provider-reported inputTokens/outputTokens are stored per call (benchmarks/src/evaluate.ts:91-92; benchmarks/results/accuracy/models/*) but the reports do not use them and no in-repo comparison between tokenizer counts and provider counts exists; the stored records contain no cache-related fields.

claim_checks.claim: 'Total evaluations: 244 questions x 6 formats x 4 models = 5,856 LLM calls' (README.md:446)
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the README: the task generator skips CSV for datasets that do not support CSV (benchmarks/scripts/accuracy-benchmark.ts:25-39, skip at 31-32), and the README itself shows CSV answering only 109 of 244 questions per model (README.md:228,254,236-241 '/436'). Calls issued = 4 x (244 x 5 + 109) = 5,316, not 5,856; the README figure is a formula that over-counts by 540 (benchmarks/src/report.ts:291-292,324).

claim_checks.claim: encodeLines/CLI give 'memory-efficient streaming'; 'Peak memory usage scales with data depth, not total size' (README.md:727-738; docs/cli/index.md:117-142)
claim_checks.evidence: Output side and decode side stream: encodeLines is a generator (packages/toon/src/index.ts:109-118; encoders.ts), and decode reads lines and emits events to a JSON text stream (packages/cli/src/utils.ts:80-105; conversion.ts:72-95,97-127). But CLI encode reads the whole input and JSON.parses it (conversion.ts:21-25; utils.ts:28-33), and encodeLines first builds a fully normalized copy of the input (index.ts:110; normalize.ts:10-92), so peak memory scales with input size on encode, contrary to docs/cli/index.md:142. `--stats` also builds the full TOON string (conversion.ts:38; acknowledged at docs/cli/index.md:144-146).

claim_checks.claim: 'Tab delimiters buy further token savings' (README.md:787; docs/reference/api.md:714)
claim_checks.evidence: No in-repo benchmark varies the delimiter: the benchmark TOON format calls encodeToon(data) with the default comma (benchmarks/src/formats.ts:44-50) and grep of benchmarks/ finds 'delimiter' only in the primer text (formats.ts:47). The option itself exists (packages/cli/src/index.ts:37-41; packages/toon/src/index.ts:201-210). The docs word it as 'often' more efficient (docs/cli/index.md:217).

packages/toon/src/decode/scanner.ts:54-59 drops lines whose first non-space character is '#' before blank-line tracking and validation (not when a tab is in the indentation, line 57); conformance fixtures 'comments' run in packages/toon/test/decode.test.ts:23. Encoders never emit comments: strings starting with '#' are quoted (packages/toon/src/shared/validation.ts:79-81) and rawString rejects comment-like lines (packages/toon/src/encode/raw-string.ts:4-6,19-21). Consequence: hand-written comments are dropped on decode.

risks: Scope: nothing here measures provider usage or reads Claude Code/Codex logs, and no input/output/cache-creation/cache-read token accounting exists. A repo search for .claude/codex/.jsonl/cache_read/input_tokens hit only repo descriptions in benchmarks/data/github-repos.json. Reductions are reported as estimator or tokenizer counts: CLI `--stats` uses tokenx over the raw input text (packages/cli/src/conversion.ts:47-59) and the benchmarks use gpt-tokenizer counts of primer + data (benchmarks/src/report.ts:25-44). Per-call provider inputTokens/outputTokens are stored (benchmarks/src/evaluate.ts:91-92) but unused in the reports and carry no cache fields.

Evidence quality: every published figure comes from the project's own harness; no third-party replication is cited, and docs/reference/efficiency-formalization.md is an analytical byte-count model, not a measurement. The runs use 4 small/fast models with reasoning disabled (benchmarks/src/evaluate.ts:23-28,70; README.md:441-446) and mostly generated, faker-seeded datasets plus one real GitHub-repos set (benchmarks/src/datasets.ts:3,5-6). Accuracy gaps vs JSON sit inside the reported intervals (README.md:215-225,282). The 42.6% headline is against pretty-printed JSON; TOON is +1.6% larger than compact JSON on the mixed-structure total, +19.9% on semi-uniform logs and +5.9% vs CSV on flat data (README.md:477,508,547). No latency figures are published (README.md:160-162). The README's 5,856-call total overstates the 5,316 calls the code issues (benchmarks/scripts/accuracy-benchmark.ts:25-39).

Recoverability caveats: round-trip is lossless only for the JSON data model after normalization (-0 -> 0; NaN/Infinity/undefined/function/symbol -> null; Date -> ISO string; BigInt > 2^53 -> string: packages/toon/src/encode/normalize.ts:43-91). Numbers are IEEE-754 doubles with silent rounding (docs/reference/api.md:343), JS reorders integer-like keys (docs/reference/api.md:635), lone surrogates throw on encode (normalize.ts:94-117), and comments are dropped on decode (packages/toon/src/decode/scanner.ts:54-59). The CLI runs JSON.parse before encoding (packages/cli/src/conversion.ts:25), so original text formatting is not recoverable. The repo contains no mechanism for storing, hashing or restoring originals.

Scale: CLI encode reads the whole input, JSON.parses it and normalizes a full copy before streaming output (packages/cli/src/conversion.ts:21-25; packages/toon/src/index.ts:110), so memory grows with input size, contrary to docs/cli/index.md:142; `--stats` also builds the whole TOON string (conversion.ts:38).

Platform: CI covers one OS and one Node version (ubuntu-slim, Node 24: .github/workflows/ci.yml:20,31-34). Neither published manifest sets `engines`, `os` or `cpu`, no minimum Node version is documented, and there is no macOS/Windows/WSL mention. Output is ESM-only (packages/toon/package.json:26-31). CLI tests execute src/entry.ts directly with node (packages/cli/test/utils.ts:15,144-147; packages/cli/package.json:33).

Maintenance and stability: the format is self-described as 'stable, but also an idea in progress' (README.md:17-18). The spec and conformance fixtures live in a separate repo/package consumed at test time (SPEC.md:3; packages/toon/package.json:40-42; packages/toon/test/utils.ts:15-19) and that package's license was not examined here. Several other official-language ports are listed as 'In Development' (docs/ecosystem/implementations.md:15-17). Single named copyright holder (LICENSE:3). Dev toolchain is on very recent majors (TypeScript ^6.0.3, Vite ^8.1.5, ESLint ^10.8.0, pnpm@11.17.0: package.json:6,19-30).

Release and supply chain: no SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING or CODEOWNERS. The release job (contents: write, id-token: write) runs unpinned `npx changelogithub` and `npm install -g npm@latest` before `pnpm -r publish --no-git-checks` (.github/workflows/release.yml:17-19,38-50). GitHub Actions are pinned by major tag, not commit SHA (ci.yml:24-41; release.yml:23-36). No checksums, signatures or explicit provenance step exist in the repo. Mitigations present: pnpm trustPolicy no-downgrade and restricted build scripts (pnpm-workspace.yaml:4-16), --frozen-lockfile installs (ci.yml:49), persist-credentials: false in CI (ci.yml:25-27).

Integration scope: no MCP server, HTTP API, Claude Code/Codex plugin, hook or skill, and no non-TypeScript SDK in this repo. The MCP proxy named in the README (Tooner) is a separate third-party project that was not examined (README.md:797; docs/ecosystem/tools-and-playgrounds.md:51-55).
